title: Phase 0: de-risk gdstrict before building
description: Three spikes that de-risk the gdstrict plan before committing real implementation work. See PLAN.md section 3 (Phase 0). All three must produce a go/no-go signal: grammar currency, strict-mode warning extraction, and the doc-IR formatter approach. Blocks Phase 1.

title: Spike: tree-sitter-gdscript grammar currency on Godot 4.5
description:
Round-trip a corpus of real Godot 4.5 .gd files through tree-sitter-gdscript and confirm the grammar covers modern syntax.

Cover: typed Dictionary[K,V], Array[T], @annotations, lambdas, await/signal, match patterns, static vars/functions, backslash continuations, multiline strings.

Accept: zero parse errors across the corpus, OR a documented list of grammar gaps with an upstream-fix/vendor-patch plan. This is the single biggest technical risk (PLAN.md section 7.1).

Output: a short findings note + the test corpus committed under fixtures/.

title: Spike: extract strict-mode warnings from Godot headless
description:
Prove that 'godot --headless --check-only --debug --path <project> --script <file.gd>' emits parseable analyzer warnings (UNSAFE_*, UNTYPED_DECLARATION, INFERRED_DECLARATION) on a sample project with deliberately unsafe/untyped code.

Godot docs only promise --check-only parses for errors; warning output is NOT a stable public API. This spike decides whether stderr-parsing is a viable committed path.

Accept: a Rust function that returns structured { file, line, col, code, message } from a known-bad file; per-file latency measured; note the Godot version pinned. Verify behavior with autoload/addon singletons present (known crash risk).

title: Spike: doc-IR formatter prototype with auto-wrapping
description:
Throwaway prototype of the Wadler/Prettier-style document IR (Group, Indent, Line, SoftLine, Text) + width-aware renderer, on one hard wrapping case: a long call chain / argument list that must wrap to one element per line at line-length 100.

Goal: confirm doc-IR over Topiary (auto-wrap needs real layout control). Validate the magic-trailing-comma behavior and idempotency on the case.

Accept: prototype wraps the case correctly and is idempotent (format(format(x)) == format(x)) on it. Decision recorded: doc-IR vs Topiary.

title: Phase 1: Formatter MVP
description: The 'black for Godot' formatter end to end. Lower the tree-sitter CST to the doc IR (engine already built in Phase 0), attach comments/trivia, normalize blank lines, tab-indent, and ship format / format --check / format --diff with golden + idempotency gates. Ships value standalone before strict mode exists. See PLAN.md section 3 (Phase 1).

title: CST -> Doc lowering
description: The bulk of the formatter: walk the tree-sitter CST (gdstrict-syntax) and emit the doc IR (gdstrict-format::doc). Cover statements, expressions, calls, arrays/dicts, control flow, func/class defs, annotations, match. Reuse the existing doc::Group/Indent/Line/IfBreak primitives and the call() wrapping pattern. Output must round-trip-parse.

title: Comment and trivia attachment
description: Attach comments, blank lines, and whitespace trivia to CST nodes and thread them through the doc IR so they survive formatting. This is precisely where gdformat breaks (CommentPersistenceViolation) — make it a first-class concern with golden tests: leading/trailing/inline comments, doc comments, blank-line runs.

title: Blank-line normalization + tab indentation
description: GDScript is tab-indented by convention: make doc::INDENT emit a tab in GDScript mode (Phase 0 used spaces). Normalize blank lines per the style guide (max 1 inside funcs, 2 between top-level defs, trim trailing/leading).

title: Force-break on input magic trailing comma
description: black/ruff behavior: if the source already has a trailing comma in a collection/arg list, force the group to break (expanded form) even if it would fit flat. Phase 0 only emits the trailing comma when broken; this wires the input comma to drive the break decision.

title: gdstrict-cli: format, --check, --diff
description: Stand up the gdstrict-cli crate (clap). Commands: format (rewrite in place), format --check (exit 1 if any file would change), format --diff (unified diff, no writes). Proper exit codes for CI/pre-commit. Walk paths, skip ignored files.

title: Golden fixtures + idempotency CI gate
description: fixtures/format/*.{in,out}.gd golden pairs. CI test that formats every fixture TWICE and asserts no change on the second pass — idempotency is the gdformat bug class we gate on. Wire into cargo test.

title: Config discovery: gdstrict.toml + ignores
description: Nearest gdstrict.toml walking up from each file (black/ruff style). Only knob: line-length (default 100). Respect .gdignore and gitignore. --config and --line-length flags override.

title: Acceptance: format a real Godot game repo
description: Run gdstrict format over a large real Godot project; assert output still parses via tree-sitter AND godot --check-only (no broken code), and double-format is a no-op. Phase 1 ship gate (PLAN.md section 3).

title: Phase 2: Syntactic linter
description: Reimplement the useful gdlint style rules on our CST (no Godot needed). Naming, dead/redundant code, structure rules + the lint command + per-rule tests. Deferred behind the formatter since GDQuest already covers style linting. See PLAN.md section 2.3.

title: gdstrict-lint: rule engine + framework
description: Stand up gdstrict-lint: a rule trait + CST visitor + diagnostic collection on top of gdstrict-syntax. No Godot needed. Each rule is independently testable with positive/negative cases.

title: Lint: naming convention rules
description: snake_case funcs/vars/args, PascalCase classes/enums, CONSTANT_CASE consts, signal naming. Mirror gdlint's name checks.

title: Lint: dead/redundant code rules
description: unused-argument, unnecessary-pass, expression-not-assigned, no-else-return, no-elif-return, comparison-with-itself, duplicated-load.

title: Lint: structure rules
description: class-definitions-order, private-method-call, max-line-length, function-arguments-number, max-public-methods.

title: gdstrict-cli: lint command
description: Wire 'gdstrict lint [paths]' into the CLI: run syntactic rules only (no Godot), respect config (enable/disable per rule), aggregate diagnostics, exit codes.

title: Phase 3: Strict mode
description: Productionize the Godot-analyzer driver (prototyped in Phase 0). Inject warning settings, run files concurrently, aggregate format+lint+strict in the check command, map warnings to error|warn|off with a strict preset, graceful no-Godot fallback, version-gated classifier. The novel differentiator. See PLAN.md section 2.4.

title: Strict: inject warning settings (don't trust project.godot)
description: gdstrict should enforce the warning set it cares about rather than trusting the project's config. Inject/override [debug] gdscript/warnings/* (e.g. via a temp project override or --debug args) so unsafe/untyped warnings are on regardless of the target project. Builds on Phase 0 gdstrict-strict.

title: Strict: benchmark whole-project vs per-file vs batch harness
description: Phase 0 follow-up: compare per-file invocation vs a single whole-project --check-only load vs a throwaway .gd batch-validation harness. Pick the fastest viable approach for CI-scale projects.

title: Strict: bounded concurrent worker pool
description: Run per-file Godot invocations concurrently with a bounded pool (~cpu-2). Phase 0 measured ~0.15s/run; serial is too slow on big projects. Handle per-file crashes gracefully without failing the whole run.

title: Strict: warning->severity config + strict preset
description: gdstrict.toml maps each warning code to error|warn|off (the project-wide warnings-as-errors enforcement Godot lacks). 'strict' preset enables UNTYPED_DECLARATION, INFERRED_DECLARATION, UNSAFE_* family, RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED as errors.

title: Strict: version-gate the message classifier
description: Godot prints warning messages, not codes; classify_warning maps message->code. Templates are stable per Godot version but not a public API (#12548 open). Detect Godot version and select the matching classifier table; test against pinned releases.

title: gdstrict-cli: check command (format+lint+strict)
description: 'gdstrict check [paths]' aggregates format-check + lint + strict into one report with unified exit codes. Graceful no-Godot fallback: if Godot is enabled but absent, exit non-zero as a config error; skip strict only on --no-strict. Binary discovery: --godot, GODOT env, PATH.

title: Strict acceptance: untyped fixture fails, clean passes
description: Fixture project with untyped/unsafe code -> check exits non-zero with exact warning codes; clean typed project -> exit 0. Pin Godot version in CI; test the no-Godot fallback path.

title: Phase 4: Distribution and DX
description: Make it adoptable: pre-commit hook, GitHub Action, prebuilt binaries (cargo-dist) for Linux/macOS/Windows, VS Code integration, docs/README. See PLAN.md section 3 (Phase 4).

title: pre-commit hook
description: .pre-commit-hooks.yaml entries for gdstrict format --check and gdstrict check, so users can drop it into .pre-commit-config.yaml.

title: GitHub Action
description: A reusable GitHub Action that installs gdstrict (+ optionally Godot) and runs format --check / lint / check in CI.

title: Prebuilt binaries via cargo-dist
description: cargo-dist release pipeline producing static binaries for Linux/macOS/Windows + install script. The single-binary distribution promise.

title: VS Code integration
description: Format-on-save task / extension config pointing at the gdstrict binary.

title: Docs site / README
description: User-facing README + docs: install, config (gdstrict.toml), the strict preset, CI setup, comparison to gdformat/GDQuest. Promote PLAN.md content into real docs.
